The api died because the `report-export` job filled the disk it shares with the database. Starting at 03:05:00 the job wrote a 512 MB CSV to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` every 12 seconds, 40 files (about 20 GB) by 03:12:48. The disk warning hit 91% at 03:09:03 and 99% at 03:13:30. At 03:14:00 the database failed with "could not extend file … No space left on device", the api aborted its transaction, shut down its worker pool and exited with status 1 at 03:14:06.

It never came back: the proxy logged "upstream api refused connection" every two minutes from 03:16:00 until 05:28:00, and the log ends at 05:29:57 with the api still down, so nothing restarted it. Web and proxy requests kept returning 200 throughout. The cache "slow command" warnings are unrelated, as they run at the same rate from 02:00 onwards.

To recover, free space by deleting or moving the `part-*.csv` files in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, then start the api. To stop a repeat, make the export write to a different volume from the database or cap its output.

The log does not show what launched the export, and nothing in this repo references `report-export`, so I could not trace why it ran or produced that much. The log's timestamps are also 2026-03-09, not last night, so check this is the file you meant.
